claims.text: GA-ASI publicly describes a DAA architecture combining cooperative surveillance sources such as TCAS/ADS-B with an air-to-air radar for non-cooperative aircraft.
claims.scope: GA-ASI vendor description; architecture claim only
claims.challenge: Obtain current configuration and independent approval records; vendor architecture does not prove performance or certification.

claims.text: The FAA/GA-ASI 2022 sensor-model-validation report describes flight testing with ATAR, ADS-B and active-surveillance data and comparison with simulation models.
claims.challenge: Inspect the associated flight-test and data-analysis reports and avoid treating model validation as system certification.

claims.text: The public GA-ASI pages inspected do not establish that a GA-ASI DAA/ATAR TSO-C211/C212 authorization was issued; they contain target or on-track language, while the FAA report is a research report.
claims.challenge: Search FAA DRS for article-specific authorization letters and request the current approval holder/model; absence from inspected pages is not proof of non-issuance.

claims.text: FAA explains that a TSO authorization approves manufacture of an article to a minimum performance standard and does not by itself approve installation and use on a particular aircraft.
claims.challenge: Check the specific aircraft type-certificate or STC installation approval for any product-specific claim.

claims.text: FAA Order 8100.18A lists TSO-C211 for DAA systems and TSO-C212 for air-to-air radar for traffic surveillance.
claims.challenge: A title listing does not show current effectiveness, authorization holders, or installation approvals.

claims.text: The inspected FAA draft TSO-C212a defines radar equipment intended to detect and generate tracks for airborne traffic, including non-cooperative traffic, and identifies separate installation approval.
claims.challenge: Confirm final TSO revision and effective date before publication; do not treat draft MPS as an approval.

claims.text: FAA's AI safety roadmap distinguishes static learned AI, whose updated versions require safety assurance, from learning AI that changes during operation and therefore requires an assurance strategy addressing the learning process itself.
claims.challenge: The roadmap is not a binding certification rule; verify later FAA policy and project-specific issue papers.

claims.text: FAA's roadmap identifies runtime assurance, formal/numerical methods, system-level testing, explainability and black-box validation as research or method-development topics for AI safety assurance.
claims.challenge: Research agenda language does not establish that any method is accepted or sufficient for a flight-critical AI function.

claims.text: EASA's Issue 2 landing-page summary says its guidance addresses learning assurance, AI explainability and Level 2 human-AI teaming; the linked PDF was not inspected in this lane.
claims.challenge: Capture and inspect the full Issue 2 PDF before making detailed requirements claims.

claims.text: EASA published a Proposed Issue 3 AI Concept Paper page dated June 3, 2026; its proposed status and uninspected PDF mean no detailed Issue 3 requirements are established here.
claims.challenge: Retrieve the PDF and comment-response document and determine whether a final issue supersedes it.

claims.text: The UK CAA's CAP3127 response describes DAA policy development as a test phase and proposes assurance of reliability, integrity, availability and performance for BVLOS operations.
claims.challenge: Check the CAA's 2026 policy publication and any applicant-specific approvals; consultation response is not final authorization.

claims.text: The FAA announced in September 2023 that Zipline was authorized for scoped Salt Lake City commercial package deliveries BVLOS without visual observers; this does not establish a DAA equipment TSO or unrestricted flight authority.
claims.challenge: Obtain the linked approval letters and conditions, then distinguish Part 135, exemption, COA/OpSpecs, aircraft approval and any DAA equipment approval.

claims.text: FAA's BEYOND status page says it approved a Zipline change submission in February 2023 to enable DAA software within the mode-C veil, while providing no full technical approval package in the page itself.
claims.challenge: Retrieve the change submission, operating limitations and associated safety analysis before describing its assurance evidence.

claims.text: A UK Ministry of Defence announcement describes Protector as intended for certification to NATO and UK safety standards and operation in UK and European civilian airspace; it is not the underlying certificate or civil operating authorization.
claims.challenge: Locate the Military Type Certificate, MAA scope, aircraft configuration and any civil CAA operational permission; military certification cannot be generalized to civil certification.
